name: layered-redraw
description: Incubation prototype for non-destructive semantic-layer artwork and cinematic 3D scene construction; canonical runtime capabilities are upstreamed to VULCA SDK as reviewed Effect Packs.

interface.shortDescription: Redraw in editable layers or stage cinematic 3D scenes.
interface.longDescription: Turn RGB references, optional depth, and an art-direction conversation into artwork with stable semantic layers, or stage screenplay-driven scenes in the experimental Three.js Scene Builder. Raw evidence stays immutable while the 2D workflow retains masks, recoverable history, quality gates, hybrid sources, and OpenRaster round trips. The 3D workflow adds hierarchical characters, spline cameras, arc-length motion, semantic object anchors, replaceable asset bindings, and a deterministic intent boundary for future intelligent agents.
defaultPrompt: Interview me, then redraw this photo as editable SVG layers.
Use Guided mode and show me composition-first design presets for this photo.
Use Art Direction mode so I can control proportion, space, form, value, and colour.
Register this RGB source, estimate relative depth, and use my prompt to plan 8–12 semantic layers.
Pair this RGB image with its supplied depth map, then keep the subject independently editable.
Generate A/B/C parameterized design proofs, let me lock one, then promote it to production.
Use raster-layered mode to generate editable PNG layers from this photo.
Create GBA warm-narrative pixel art with editable semantic layers.
Open my layered project and change only the selected or masked layers.
Use $stage-in-3d to stage my screenplay with smooth cameras, continuous character motion, and semantic object interactions.
